clue.text: Rose Marie or Eliza prior to transformation

blocks.note: a rose is a kind of flower
Marie is a girl's name, so it stands for a girl

explanation.surface: Two heroines of musicals, Rose Marie and Eliza Doolittle, compared before their makeovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose Marie' reads as one operetta title, but it splits into two words that each give a piece. Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady sells flowers in Covent Garden before Higgins remakes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Before Professor Higgins taught her to speak like a lady, Eliza earned her living selling blooms on the London streets.

clue.text: Refuse to eat quickly

blocks.note: first meaning: go without food
second meaning: at speed

explanation.surface: Someone declines food in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to abstain from food, and the adverb means rapidly or at high speed.

clue.text: Column reference mark

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall tapering stone pillar
second meaning: the dagger sign used in print to point to a footnote

explanation.surface: A typographer's mark used to point to a column of text.
explanation.walkthrough: The dagger symbol in printing is also called an obelus or obelisk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a four-sided monumental stone pillar and the printer's dagger sign for footnotes.

clue.text: Brave to go into opening by force

blocks.note: to enter is to go into
prising a lid is levering it open

explanation.surface: It takes courage to break in somewhere by force.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person shows boldness and initiative in taking on new ventures, so is bold or brave.

clue.text: Neat result of using the needles

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for a cow, here a breed of dairy cattle
second meaning: a thick knitted woollen sweater

explanation.surface: A tidy piece of knitting comes off the needles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is an old word for cattle; the breed comes from the Channel Island of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a breed of dairy cow from the Channel Islands and a fisherman's knitted wool jumper.

clue.text: Enthusiastic artist on call

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A keen painter waits by the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring to go means eager and impatient to start, so the word conveys keen enthusiasm.

clue.text: Note airmen count in German

blocks.note: G is one of the musical notes
the Royal Air Force, Britain's airmen

explanation.surface: Someone notes how many airmen there are, tallying them in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb for tallying, but it is the noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: Graf is the German title of nobility equivalent to an English earl or continental count.

clue.text: Gaining knowledge in University

blocks.note: first meaning: learning from books
second meaning: the university in a Berkshire town west of London

explanation.surface: A student learning things at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a student at college; the second meaning is the University of Reading, in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying books is how one learns, and Reading is also the name of an English university town.

clue.text: Ideal mount for the little people

definitions.text: Ideal mount for the little people

blocks.note: surface reading: a perfect horse or pony to ride
setter's reading: the little people are the fey folk of folklore, and also small children, who ride a tiny bicycle

explanation.walkthrough: A fairy cycle was a small child's bicycle sold in Britain from the 1920s; the little people are both children and the fey folk.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small child's bicycle, a ride suited to children and, by its name, to the elves of folklore.

clue.text: Adored one shows taste where fashionable

blocks.note: sweet is one of the basic tastes of the tongue
the heart of town is the centre, where the fashionable go

explanation.surface: A beloved person reveals good taste in a smart setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is loose: the heart of a place is its smart centre, where it is all happening. 'Taste' looks like discernment but names a flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is dearly loved by another is their darling or beloved, the usual term of endearment.

clue.text: Dress for Royal handmaid in retirement

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the name is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendants in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A palace maid who has retired needs something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal is Cleopatra: Shakespeare gives her two maids, Iras and Charmian.
explanation.definitionFit: The sari is the draped garment worn by women in India and South Asia, a single length of cloth.

clue.text: No alternative to moving tractor in a fair form of defence

indicators.note: no means without, so the following word's letters are taken away
letters that are moving shift about into a new order

blocks.note: or is the word offering an alternative
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: With no other choice, a tractor driven round a funfair becomes a kind of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No alternative' removes OR from the words that follow, and the remaining twelve letters are shuffled. 'In a fair' looks like setting but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns and missiles aimed at hostile planes are a military system for protecting against attack from the air.

clue.text: Landing place over the water

blocks.note: surface reading: a spot on a staircase or an airfield where one alights
setter's reading: a structure built out above the sea where boats land passengers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' suggests a staircase or an aircraft; here it is boats putting people ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty on stilts projects out above the sea so vessels can moor alongside and passengers disembark.

clue.text: Suitable diary subject for the Grossmiths

definitions.text: Suitable diary subject for the Grossmiths

blocks.note: surface reading: someone worth writing a journal about
setter's reading: the Grossmith brothers wrote The Diary of a Nobody, so their subject is a nobody

explanation.surface: Who would make a good subject for a diary by the Grossmith brothers?
explanation.walkthrough: George and Weedon Grossmith wrote The Diary of a Nobody (1892), the comic journal of the clerk Charles Pooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no importance, which is exactly what the word for an insignificant person means.

clue.text: Pardon graduate coming up with explanation

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
a solution explains a problem

explanation.surface: A graduate asks forgiveness and arrives with an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon' looks like an apology, but it is a noun meaning forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal release from guilt or sin, the remission granted by a priest, so a pardon.

clue.text: Sources of hot money?

blocks.note: surface reading: speculative cash that moves quickly between markets, or stolen funds
setter's reading: dough is slang for money, and warm loaves come from the places that bake bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot money' is a finance term; the question mark signals the pun on dough, slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread shops produce hot dough, and dough is everyday slang for money, so they are sources of it.

clue.text: Small boat needed for boarding hydrofoil

indicators.note: the letters are needed from inside the words that follow, which supply them as they stand

blocks.note: the run of letters straddles the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A little boat is required to get onto a hydrofoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tender ferrying passengers out, but the boat is concealed in boarDING HYdrofoil.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small open rowing or sailing boat, often used as a tender to reach larger vessels.

clue.text: No credit for researcher resolved to practise

indicators.note: no means without, so those letters are struck out of the word
something resolved is broken down and worked into a new form

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unacknowledged scientist decides to keep going over the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' looks like decided, but it signals rearranging what remains after CR goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to go over a performance repeatedly in preparation, the same as practising it.

clue.text: Bosses are out to take over

indicators.note: things that are out are put out of place, so the word's letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The managers have gone on strike, or been ousted, so someone else can seize control.
explanation.definitionFit: To preoccupy the mind completely is to take it over, the sense of a thought dominating a person.

clue.text: Outlook good for established festival

blocks.note: set means established or fixed
a fair is a festive gathering

explanation.surface: Fine weather forecast for a long-running fete.
explanation.walkthrough: Set fair is the barometer reading for settled fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes weather or prospects that look settled and favourable, so a promising forecast.

clue.text: Have a hand in genuine forgiveness

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: genuine means real
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Taking part in a sincere act of pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: Remitting a debt or sin means cancelling it, so remittal is pardon or release from a penalty.

clue.text: Crackling sound made by paper when cut

indicators.note: cutting shortens something, so the tail of the name is trimmed off

blocks.note: The Thunderer is the old nickname of The Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Paper rustles as it is sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own paper, The Times, has long been nicknamed The Thunderer; cutting drops its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise following lightning crackles and rumbles across the sky, a booming crackling noise from a storm.

clue.text: The French are here?

blocks.note: surface reading: the article la or le, or the people of France arriving
setter's reading: from a British view, the French live overseas, in foreign parts

explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' tempts the solver to write LE or LA; it means the people, who from Britain are across the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To someone in Britain, France is a foreign country, so its people live overseas in foreign lands.

clue.text: Not to be up to comprehending X is indefensible

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to grasp or include, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: not up to a task means incapable
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Failing to understand the letter X is inexcusable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehending' looks like understanding, but here it means taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that cannot be held or defended against attack or argument is untenable.

clue.text: Firm in the lead makes take-over

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
a side that is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A company ahead of its rivals launches a takeover bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective but is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden seizure of power from a government, a coup d'état, is a forcible takeover.

clue.text: Repeat going up the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: to redo something is to repeat it

explanation.surface: Travelling upstream along the river once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder flows along the border between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major central European waterway running to the Baltic, so it is a river.

clue.text: Duke leaves seat for him

definitions.note: a man's name, standing for any male person

indicators.note: when someone leaves he goes away, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
a divan is a backless couch or seat

explanation.surface: A duke vacates his chair to make room for another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' could be foliage; here the duke departs from the seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a common Russian male name, so it can stand for a particular man referred to as him.

clue.text: Epithet for bridge or piano duet -

blocks.note: first meaning: a card game played by four people, each holding a hand
second meaning: music for two pianists at one keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is a card game for four players; a piano duet uses two players' pairs of hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both a game with four players' hands of cards and keyboard music played by two people together.

clue.text: Fellow loses a point to par

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so letters are dropped from the name

blocks.note: Norman is a man's name, so a fellow
taken as written
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A golfer drops a point and falls back to the course's standard score.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like golf, but par is the definition meaning the usual standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the expected standard or average level, which is the norm.

clue.text: Soldier of fortune coming to the city with the King

blocks.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, Abraham's home, the crossword's favourite city
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A mercenary arrives in the capital alongside the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of fortune is a person who seeks wealth through risky enterprises, often fighting for pay.
